proof_summary: Lucas congruences pair the summands indexed by \(k\) and \(p+k\) with opposite signs, showing both sequences vanish modulo \(p\) at every \(p+r\) with \(0\le r<p\); at \(p-1\), \(\binom{p-1}{k}\equiv(-1)^k\), giving boundary values \(1\) for the first sum and \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\) for the second, where central-binomial vanishing leaves only the midpoint. Thus each Hankel matrix is anti-triangular modulo \(p\), and expanding its determinant along the last nonzero anti-diagonal gives the requisite sign times the \(p\)-th power of that boundary value, which simplifies to the two claimed residues.
